title: Blueprint `sk-prop-sp-composition`, case of an open immersion: **compatibility of purity with composition with an open immersion**: for `f` smooth of
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $k$ a field of positive prime characteristic $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf N$, and let $j:Y\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion. Assume also that $h=j\circ f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, as in the recorded Lean declaration [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-open-immersion, sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the finite-extension-valued condensed coefficient convention [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the bounded constructible category of modules over $B_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, $\mathbf1_T$ for its coefficient unit, and $\iota_T:\mathcal C_T\hookrightarrow D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ for its full inclusion [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Use the chosen compact-support adjunctions $F_v=Rv_!\dashv G_v=Rv^!$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek, sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek]. Let $\gamma_v:\iota_XG_v\mathbf1_{\operatorname{target}(v)}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(d)[2d]$ for $v=f,h$ be the specified normalized smooth purity isomorphisms of [def-pur-condensed-smooth-purity-iso], with the Tate construction of [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists].

Let $c_{j,f}:G_h\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fG_j$ be the counit mate of the canonical proper/open compact-support composition $F_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_jF_f$; in the live library it is $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleUpperShriekComp\_padicAlgCl}(\ell,f,j)$. Let $u_j:G_j\mathbf1_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_Y$ be the canonical comparison with exact open inverse image followed by its monoidal unit comparison; it is $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleUpperShriekUnitIso\_padicAlgCl}(\ell,j)$, not an arbitrarily chosen purity isomorphism. Then the equality of isomorphisms in the ambient module-derived category is
$$\gamma_h=\gamma_f\circ\iota_X\bigl(G_f(u_j)\circ c_{j,f,\mathbf1_Z}\bigr).$$
Here the canonical comparisons are normalized by their adjunction counits, not just by their endpoints [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek, def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction].

proof.text: Work first over $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, $n\ge1$, on ordinary etale modules. The schemes are Noetherian by finite type over the field, and the separated finite-type maps admit compactifications. Thus the arbitrary-ground-field finite purity construction applies to $f,h$ and $j$. Denote its orientation by $a_{v,n}:v_n^\times A_{n,\operatorname{target}(v)}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ for $v=f,h$. The construction specifies the first diagonal base-change arrow, the normalized Rees deformation arrow, and the integration arrow, rather than allowing arbitrary identifications. Write $r_n=h_n^\times A_{n,Z}\xrightarrow{c_n}f_n^\times j_n^\times A_{n,Z}\xrightarrow{f_n^\times(u_{j,n})}f_n^\times A_{n,Y}$, where the composition map is the counit mate of compact-support composition and $u_{j,n}$ is exact open restriction at the constant sheaf.

source.place: Finite coefficients: the orientation and the composite adjunction

proof.text: Compare the two finite orientations. Since $j$ identifies $Y$ with an open subscheme of $Z$, its diagonal is the identity on that subscheme. Explicitly, two maps to $Y$ with equal composites to $Z$ agree, including their maps of structure sheaves, by restriction to this open. Consequently $X\times_YX\to X\times_ZX$ is the canonical isomorphism preserving both projections and the diagonal. The diagonal ideal, its extended-Rees algebra, the homogeneous cone-to-normal-bundle map, and the vector-bundle projection with zero section are therefore the same for $f$ and $h$. The deformation and Kummer integration factors in the displayed construction of the finite purity node are identical. For the first factor, paste the base-change square for $h$ with the open square for $j$; compact-support exchanges respect this pasting and composition. The mate-pasting identity, followed by the open counit, identifies the diagonal base-change arrow for $h$ with the one for $f$ composed with $r_n$. Thus $a_{h,n}=a_{f,n}r_n$. At the coefficient unit the tensor formula in the finite purity construction is the unit identification: its transpose is the counit itself. Taking inverses gives $r_n\gamma_{h,n}=\gamma_{f,n}$. This argument uses the same diagonal pair, not a comparison of unrelated orientations or a finite-field descent.

source.place: Orientation, finite coefficients; tensor maps at the constant object

proof.text: Pass to finite pro-etale coefficients using the specified site comparisons. The proper/open composition comparison commutes with ordinary-etale/pro-etale transport by the composition equation of the finite compact-support site-coherence node. Taking counit mates preserves this equation. The finite smooth-purity node defines its pro-etale maps by precisely this transport, including the open and proper counits, so the equation $r_n\gamma_{h,n}=\gamma_{f,n}$ holds for these actual pro-etale maps. Its coefficient comparisons obey the quotient cocycle. For $j$ the finite purity node's dimension-zero normalization is the etale adjunction, hence $u_{j,n}$ is the canonical open-unit map in this calculation.

source.place: Finite coefficients and their passage to towers

proof.text: For every $n\ge m\ge1$ take $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z\to B=\mathbf Z/\ell^m\mathbf Z$ and the smooth maps $f,j$. Every input in $\Dctf$ has a bounded constructible etale origin with the same Tor interval [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. The composition equation of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], applied to that origin, gives the finite $b$ identity $b_hS\alpha_A=\alpha_BF_{j,B}(b_f)b_jF_{f,A}$ for the specified pro-etale proper/open compositors (its refinement equation returns to the fixed compactifications, identified with the compositors of Step 1 by site coherence); [lem-sp-finite-adjoint-compositor-transposes] turns it into the transposed $c$ identity for the exceptional compositors. These are exactly the hypotheses of lem-sp-tower-adjoint-compositor-realization, so that theorem gives the actual counit-preserving tower compositor and its finite evaluations. The Tate-tower theorem supplies the normalized system $M_\bullet=(A_{n,X}(d)[2d])_n$, integral unit systems $L_{T,\bullet}=(A_{n,T})_n$, completed reconstructions and common bounds. The local-freeness theorem makes each roots-of-unity line locally free of rank one; its tensor powers shifted by $[2d]$ therefore have the common Tor interval $[-2d,-2d]$. The tower-compositor theorem preserves the required uniform constructible finite-Tor subcategories, including the compact-support intermediates. Finite purity concentrates the exceptional systems in degree $-2d$ for $f,h$ and degree zero for $j$. The good-truncation clause of the reconstructed representing-pair theorem now applies: Step 3 gives the finite identification squares for the tower compositor followed by open restriction, hence gives the equality $r_\bullet\theta_h=\theta_f$ of actual system maps. Here $r_\bullet$ includes the canonical identification $j_\bullet^!L_{Z,\bullet}\cong L_{Y,\bullet}$.

source.place: Towers: compare single-degree orientation systems before reconstruction

proof.text:
Put $L_T=R\varprojlim L_{T,\bullet}$ and $M=R\varprojlim M_\bullet$. Write $P_v$ for integral compact support. For the one map $j$ choose its trivial compactification in Steps 5–6; the reconstructed-pair refinement theorem and the single-morphism realization comparison transport both traces and realization maps from the chosen compactification through a common refinement. The integral representing-pair theorem gives the actual reconstructed traces $t_f:P_fM\to L_Y$, $t_h:P_hM\to L_Z$, and $t_j:P_jL_Y\to L_Z$. For $j$, the degree-zero orientation is the open adjunction. Thus $t_j$ is the integral open counit, including the specified reduction/limit unit comparisons, as stated by the open-counit realization lemma. Transpose Step 4 under the composite tower adjunction: its counit is $\epsilon_j\mathcal F_j(\epsilon_f)$, so the resulting equality is $t_{h,\bullet}\alpha_\bullet=t_{j,\bullet}\mathcal F_j(t_{f,\bullet})$. Apply the reconstruction adjunction calculus. Its composite comparison inserts the actual counit $\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y\to1$, exactly the factor in the definition of $\alpha_R$ in the compositor-realization node. Naturality of this counit therefore gives the equality of actual integral maps
$$t_h\alpha_R=t_jP_j(t_f):P_jP_fM\longrightarrow L_Z.$$
The representing-pair formula identifies the reconstructed traces in this calculation with these $t_v$, rather than with arbitrary lifts of finite-level maps.

source.place: Reconstruct the composite counit equation before extending coefficients

proof.text:
The compositor lemma’s compactification-compatibility clause permits the trivial compactification of $j$ from Step 5 and still identifies the result with the live chosen-compactification compositor. Use $U_T$ and $a_v:U P_v\cong F_vU$ of the compositor-realization lemma, and set $T_v=U(t_v)a_v^{-1}$, with $T_j:F_jU_YL_Y\to U_ZL_Z$. That lemma supplies the previously missing equality $a_hU(\alpha_R)=\alpha_\Omega F_j(a_f)a_j$, where $\alpha_\Omega$ is precisely the inverse of the live Nagata-built LowerShriekComp. Naturality of $a_j$ at $t_f$ changes Step 5 into
$$T_h\alpha_\Omega=T_jF_j(T_f).$$
Let $\lambda_T:U_TL_T\cong\mathbf1_T$ be the specified degree-zero Tate unit. The open-counit realization lemma applies with the finite-extension-valued $B_T$, on the bounded constructible categories. Its counit equation and final unit-normalization clause give, after the canonical trivial-compactification comparison $F_j\cong j_!$,
$$\lambda_ZT_j=\epsilon_j^o\,j_!(\lambda_Y),$$
where $\epsilon_j^o:j_!\mathbf1_Y\to\mathbf1_Z$ is the open counit read through the inverse of the monoidal pullback-unit map. In particular both $\lambda_Y$ and $\lambda_Z$ are the actual units used in the definition of purity. With $\tau_v=\lambda_{\operatorname{target}(v)}T_v$, the preceding equations yield $\tau_h\alpha_\Omega=\epsilon_j^oF_j(\tau_f)$.

source.place: Realize the actual left compositor and match the two target-unit maps

proof.text:
Let $\widetilde c_v:U_XM\to G_v(U L_{\operatorname{target}(v)})$ be the representing transpose from exceptional reconstruction. The comparison used in the definition of purity is $c_v=G_v(\lambda_{\operatorname{target}(v)})\widetilde c_v$, so its transpose is exactly $\tau_v$. Let $q_j=u_j^{-1}:\mathbf1_Y\to G_j\mathbf1_Z$. Refinement coherence compares the chosen compactification with the trivial one through a common refinement, preserving the representing counit. The restricted open adjunction and counit-preserving uniqueness then show that the transpose of $q_j$ is $\epsilon_j^o$: the identification $F_j\cong j_!$ is the chosen-compactification/trivial-compactification comparison, and its conjugate followed by the monoidal unit map is the live UnitIso. This uses only the finite-extension-valued coefficient category. Under the composite adjunction, the transpose of $G_f(q_j)c_f$ is
$$\epsilon_jF_j(q_j\tau_f)=\epsilon_j^oF_j(\tau_f),$$
by naturality and the triangle identity. The transpose of $c_{j,f}c_h$ is $\tau_h\alpha_\Omega$, by the counit-mate definition of the live UpperShriekComp. Step 6 equates these transposes. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $c_{j,f}c_h=G_f(q_j)c_f$, and hence
$$G_f(u_j)c_{j,f}c_h=c_f.$$
This establishes the required equation for the normalized comparisons, including their target-unit factors. The actual mate calculation is now proved in Lean by smoothTrace_conjugate_adjunct and smoothPurityMap_comp_of_trace_transitivity, before the disputed instance. Apply the inverse composite-adjunction Hom bijection, the conjugate-counit identity and naturality of the live left compositor. For any target-unit map q, the given equation LowerShriekComp.inv;trace_h=F_j(trace_f;q);epsilon_j implies alpha_h;UpperShriekComp.hom=alpha_f;G_f(q). The argument uses the live chosen Nagata compositor and retains q explicitly. Establishing the geometric trace transitivity equation remains a separate obligation. The normalization of the open target-unit factor with an arbitrary preceding trace is now proved by smoothTrace_openComposite_counit. Functoriality separates t and the open-unit inverse, the actual open-unit counit equation removes the exceptional factor, and naturality transports the chosen left compactification comparison to the source of t. No smoothness, invertibility or assertion about smoothTrace is used in that counit calculation.

proof.text: Both constructions use the identical Tate tower on $X$. Hence its Tate realization $a:\iota_XU_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(d)[2d]$ is the same map for $f$ and $h$. By the defining formula for normalized condensed purity, $\gamma_v=a(\iota_Xc_v)^{-1}$. The equality $r c_h=c_f$ gives $(\iota_Xc_h)^{-1}=(\iota_Xc_f)^{-1}\iota_Xr$. Composing on the left with $a$ gives $\gamma_h=\gamma_f\iota_Xr$, as claimed. The shift remains $2d$ and the twist remains $d$ because the open map adds dimension zero. The complete algebraic last step is now proved in smoothPurityIso_comp_of_reconstructed_traces: take the same realized Tate object M and the same ambient Tate realization a for both maps; assume the two actual trace formulas and the reconstructed square ch.hom followed by r.hom = cf.hom. The reconstructed-trace inverse formula rewrites both purity isomorphisms. Cancel the epi ch.hom to prove ch.inv = r.hom followed by cf.inv, then apply the inclusion functor and associativity. The helper allows any comparison r, in particular the specified live exceptional compositor followed by open-unit identification. The two normalized trace formulas and the comparison square remain the preceding geometric obligations. The final native inversion, without any auxiliary reconstructed isomorphisms, is now proved by smoothPurityIso_comp_of_trace_transitivity. Supply the two actual IsIso hypotheses explicitly and the trace transitivity equation with q equal to the inverse live open-unit isomorphism. Compose the preceding purity-map equation with G_f of the open-unit hom, cancel the invertible actual alpha_h, and apply the inclusion functor. This gives exactly the original ambient formula. Neither invertibility nor the geometric trace equation is inferred from the disputed universal instance.

theorem smoothPurityIso_comp_openImmersion {Z : Over (Spec (.of k))} [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom]
    [QuasiCompact Z.hom] [IsSeparated Z.hom] (j : Y ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j.left]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (f ≫ j).left] :
    smoothPurityIso ℓ (f ≫ j) d =
      (ObjectProperty.ι _).mapIso
          ((boundedConstructibleUpperShriekComp_padicAlgCl ℓ f j).app _ ≪≫
            (boundedConstructibleUpperShriek _ ℓ f).mapIso
              (boundedConstructibleUpperShriekUnitIso_padicAlgCl ℓ j)) ≪≫
        smoothPurityIso ℓ f d :=
  sorry
